vocab.meaning: the things you have done in past jobs

examples.target: I have two years of experience.
She has a lot of experience.

vocab.meaning: a group of people who work together

examples.target: I like working in a team.

vocab.meaning: to ask for a job in a formal way

examples.target: I apply for a job online.

vocab.meaning: a good quality that you have
the money you get each month for work

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Thank you for coming. Why did you apply for this job?

glosses.meaning: to ask for a job in a formal way

dialogue.en: Thanks for being here. Why did you ask for this work?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I like the company, and I have three years of experience in this field.

glosses.meaning: the things you have done in past jobs

dialogue.en: I like the company, and I worked three years in this area.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Good. What is your biggest strength?

glosses.meaning: a good quality that you have

dialogue.en: Good. What good quality do you have most?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I learn fast, and I work well in a team.

glosses.meaning: a group of people who work together

dialogue.en: I understand new things quickly, and I work well with others.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.text: Great. We will contact you next week about the salary.

glosses.meaning: the money you get each month for work

dialogue.en: Good. We will write to you next week about the money.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. I hope you will hire me!
dialogue.en: Thanks. I hope you give me the job!

practice_words.tip: Say 'strengkth': the end has a 'th' sound
Say ik-SPEER-ee-unce: stress the second part
